claims.claim: **Recurrent minor infections in a young child usually do not mean a PID.** A healthy toddler can have 5–10 minor infections yearly, and often more if in childcare.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider PID in any child with** severe infection, more infections than expected for age, or infection by opportunistic or unusual organisms.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recurrent infection at the same site may be anatomical** — e.g. recurrent meningitis with a blood–brain barrier defect.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **In severe PIDs, early diagnosis can prevent infective complications and allows curative treatment.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History red flags:** poor growth (especially slow weight gain) · chronic diarrhoea · **four or more ear infections, or two or more serious sinus infections, in one year** · recurrent abscesses of skin or deep organs · persistent thrush after 1 year of age · antibiotics for two or more months with little effect · repeated admissions for IV antibiotics · invasive pneumococcal or meningococcal disease · severe or prolonged common infections (e.g. adenovirus).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Family history:** immunodeficiency, a previous sibling death (unexplained or from infection), or parental consanguinity.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examination:** oral candidiasis · gingivitis · persistent lymphadenopathy · chronic or severe sinusitis or otitis media · skin abscesses · clubbing · severe eczema or eczema-like rash · splenomegaly · poor muscle bulk, fat stores or nutrition.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Antibody deficiency** (e.g. XLA, CVID, specific antibody deficiency): chronic diarrhoea or malabsorption, poor growth, recurrent or severe sinusitis or otitis media, meningitis, sepsis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Combined immunodeficiency** (e.g. SCID, 22q11 deletion/DiGeorge, X-linked hyper-IgM, Wiskott-Aldrich): poor growth, absent thymus, chronic diarrhoea, recurrent sinusitis or otitis, severe nappy rash or eczema, severe oral candidiasis, severe or chronic viral infection such as EBV.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Phagocytic cell deficiency** (e.g. CGD, LAD, Chediak-Higashi, cyclic neutropenia): recurring abscesses of skin or deep organs, gingivitis, osteomyelitis, severe or recurrent pneumonia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Complement deficiency** (e.g. hereditary angioedema, specific complement deficiency): **sepsis or meningitis from encapsulated bacteria** (*N. meningitidis*, *S. pneumoniae*, Hib), recurrent angioedema.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Immune dysregulation** (e.g. ALPS, IPEX, APECED, familial HLH): endocrine disorders, chronic diarrhoea, lymphadenopathy. **Autoinflammatory disorders** (e.g. FMF, CRMO): rash, splenomegaly, recurrent fevers, inflammatory peritonitis or arthritis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First line: FBE and differential** (compare with previous results) **and a blood film** (for Howell-Jolly bodies).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After specialist consultation:** total IgG/A/M (**not IgG subclasses routinely**) · lymphocyte subsets (CD19, CD16/56, CD3, CD4, CD8) · HIV antibody.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **If SCID is suspected, assess naïve T cells (CD45RA/RO)** — CD4/CD8 counts may be normal.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Invasive meningococcal or pneumococcal disease: abdominal ultrasound for a spleen and complement studies** (e.g. CH50).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Investigate for immunodeficiency:** any child over 2 years with no clear predisposition who has invasive pneumococcal disease (meningitis, sepsis, septic arthritis, complicated pneumonia), and **every child with recurrent IPD.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Normal first-line tests but high suspicion: refer to a paediatric immunologist** for second-line testing.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not give live vaccines to a child with suspected PID** — including varicella, MMR, rotavirus and BCG.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Discuss any suspected SCID immediately with a paediatric immunologist.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the paediatric team for** severe infection or poor response to therapy, **fever in a child with known or suspected PID**, or uncertainty about whether investigation and follow-up are needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** the child is well, there is a clear management plan, and the family know when to return.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Primary immunodeficiencies' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Primary_immunodeficiencies/, retrieved 2026-09-23
